summary: Clarify residency guarantees and cross-region fallback behavior for region-pinned requests and expected latency impact
description:
Issue summary:
Customer wants a clear statement of the platform's data residency guarantees when a customer pins traffic to a specific region (eu-west) and how cross-region fallback behaves when that region has capacity constraints. They are specifically worried about: whether any customer PII or unredacted request payloads may leave the pinned region during fallback, what controls exist to prevent cross-region routing, and the expected latency implications if fallback to another region occurs.

Requested outcome:
- A precise explanation (for compliance) of whether request bodies, logs, or cache artifacts can be transferred to another region during fallback.
- Documentation pointers and console settings that enforce strict in-region residency (if available).
- Typical latency delta numbers for eu-west -> us-east fallback for streaming and non-streaming generation at 256/1024 token lengths.

Customer quote: "We need to demonstrate to our security team that pinning to eu-west prevents exfiltration of EU data except under a documented and auditable fallback that we control. Also need guidance on perf expectations in case fallback happens."
impact: Customer compliance team is delaying integration sign-off until residency/fallback behavior is documented. Potential revenue delay for Dedicated/private deployment. No active outage reported but business approval blocked.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer configured project with region pinning=eu-west in Redwood Console.
2) Sent test generation requests (streaming and non-streaming) from EU client.
3) Observed occasional 429s and backend routing debug entries showing 'fallback-route' in request trace.
4) Customer requests confirmation about payload routing and persistence when fallback occurs.
logs:
Excerpt from request trace (redacted):
- trace_id=tx-9a12e, route_attempts=[eu-west-primary, eu-west-burst, fallback-us-east-1], status=200, note=successful-on-fallback
- Console audit entry: user=devops@Nimbus, action=update:region_pin=eu-west, time=2026-03-08T14:04:22Z
Full traces linked in related_confluence_pages.
investigation_notes:
- Initial triage: routing logic is honoring 'pin=eu-west' preference but Smart Routing allows controlled fallback to compatible regions when local capacity is exhausted or when latency SLO cannot be met.
- Confirmed with routing team (see Slack thread #support-routing) that request bodies are not 'replicated' proactively to other regions; fallback involves executing the inference in the fallback region using the received request.
- KV/prefix cache: in-region cache entries are not automatically streamed to fallback region; a cache miss in eu-west will result in inference executed in fallback region without prior transfer of cached state.
- Logs and audit records: request traces and console audit logs may be stored centrally depending on tenant settings; for Private deployments customers can enable local-only audit sinks (KMS/HSM controls).
- Performance check: measured p95 generation latency delta for eu-west -> us-east fallback during a short test (internal synthetic): non-streaming 256 tokens ~ +120ms, non-streaming 1024 tokens ~ +340ms, streaming tail increases vary (client RTT dominates) — these are lab numbers and depend on instance sizing.
- Compliance note: current behavior implies request payloads are processed in fallback region (i.e., data will be present in the fallback region transiently for the duration of the inference).
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Ayesha Kapoor (Support): Created ticket after customer escalation. Attached trace exports and requested an urgent compliance statement and perf numbers.

2026-03-10 11:30 - Marco Alvarez (Routing Eng): Confirming routing behavior. Smart Routing respects pin but will fallback when eu-west lacks capacity or when a configured policy allows cross-region fallback (default is allowed for enterprise tenants). Collecting exact code paths and policy names.

2026-03-10 14:02 - Alice Chen (Security): Noted that audit sinks differ between Hosted and Private. For Hosted, logs are retained per global retention policy; for Private, we can configure local-only audit sink. Asked customer which deployment model they plan to use.

2026-03-11 08:20 - Customer (Nimbus Finance, Marco Rossi): Nimbus confirmed they aim to use Hosted (enterprise) for initial rollout. They requested an explicit statement that ROI data will not be stored outside EU persistently and asked for an opt-out of cross-region fallback until legal sign-off.

2026-03-11 13:45 - Marco Alvarez (Routing Eng): Follow-up: Provided temporary mitigation options: 1) disable automatic fallback in project settings (console flag: allow_cross_region_fallback=false) which will cause increased 429s instead of routing out-of-region; 2) configure stricter capacity thresholds and dedicated region-reserved capacity (Dedicated) to avoid fallback; 3) for Hosted, we can add a request to review tenant policy to enforce EU-only for this customer as a special case (requires SOC/Legal approval). Asked Product/Sales to escalate if needed.

2026-03-12 09:00 - Ayesha Kapoor (Support): Sent lab latency numbers and the temporary mitigation steps to customer. Asked Nimbus to confirm whether they want the console flag changed or to pursue a tenant-level policy exception.
resolution:
Workarounds provided: (A) Console setting to disable cross-region fallback (allow_cross_region_fallback=false) recommended as immediate stop-gap for compliance; customer warned this may increase 429s/failed requests under capacity pressure. (B) Suggested Dedicated reserved capacity in eu-west to prevent fallback with expected SLA. Security provided guidance: for Hosted deployments request payloads processed during fallback will exist transiently in fallback region memory/compute but are not persisted to long-term storage by default. For stricter residency, Private deployment or tenant-level policy enforcement is required.
Follow-up actions: Product to evaluate tenant-level EU-only enforcement for enterprise; Legal/Security to prepare a short compliance statement for Nimbus.
